problem.claim: Learning-rate scheduling without knowing the optimization stopping step T is difficult.

gap.claim: Schedules that avoid specifying T are reported to perform substantially worse than T-dependent schedules.

contributions.claim: Schedule-Free optimization removes learning-rate schedules and the need to specify T, while adding no hyperparameters beyond standard momentum optimizers.
The approach is derived from a theory unifying scheduling and iterate averaging.
The authors provide an open-source implementation.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors distinguish Schedule-Free optimization by eliminating schedules through a theory that connects scheduling with iterate averaging.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report state-of-the-art performance versus schedules across problems from convex optimization to large-scale deep learning.
The authors report that Schedule-Free AdamW powered their winning entry in the MLCommons 2024 AlgoPerf Algorithmic Efficiency Challenge Self-Tuning track.

narrative_sequence.summary: Existing schedules that do not require T are reported to underperform T-dependent schedules.
The paper proposes removing schedules entirely to avoid requiring T.
The approach is presented as requiring no extra hyperparameters over momentum optimizers and as following from a scheduling/iterate-averaging theory.
The authors report broad comparative performance, a competition result, and an open-source implementation.

source_observation.claim: The abstract links the schedule-free method to a unifying theory and explicitly states its hyperparameter cost relative to a standard optimizer.

lessons.interpretation: Pairing a conceptual derivation with an operational complexity statement can make a proposed optimization method easier to assess.
lessons.application: When presenting a new algorithm, connect its mechanism to a concise theoretical principle and state precisely what tuning burden it adds or removes.
lessons.exception: This framing is unsuitable when the theory or tuning comparison cannot be stated accurately from the available results.

unknowns: The abstract gives no quantitative performance values, baselines, datasets, or experimental protocols for the state-of-the-art claim.
The scope and formal guarantees of the proposed theory are unspecified.
The competition result does not identify the margin, setting details, or independently verified outcome.
